packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: fresh Claude subagents (Opus 5.5), image-only, one per packet; packets 01 and 06 sent back to the same reader for further passes on named tiles; the packet-01 reader consulted an advisor model on process only (no readings), as its response states
text:
packet-07 - unverified image-only reading (first reader)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading for this packet. I did not read packet.json.

Image set: 20 images = 4 faces, each one reduced overview (image-001, -006, -011, -016; 1340x1800) followed by four native-resolution horizontal strip tiles running top to bottom (002-005, 007-010, 012-015, 017-020).

LAYOUT SURVEY

Face 1 (overview image-001): single parchment leaf, portrait, heavily abraded and stained (looks like a former binding/wrapper surface). Text is in brown ink, very faded, Gothic textualis-type book hand, one wide block of long lines (or possibly a single column) occupying the left ~3/4 of the leaf; a narrower vertical strip at the right edge (~x 1100-1300 on the overview) is a darker, folded/creased zone with traces of text continuing into it - probably the text block running to the fold or a turn-in, damaged with tears and holes along the right edge. Top lines (about 4 lines starting y~270) are slightly darker and seem to begin with a paragraph mark or initial; a faint offset/stain of a blue letter (looks like a "C" or "E" in blue outline) sits mid-page around x 780, y 690 - possibly a blue initial bleeding through from the other side or an offset, not part of the visible text. Faint large shapes (a large initial or offset?) around y 400 and y 900-1100. Roughly 30+ lines visible from y~270 to ~1500; lower half almost entirely effaced. No running title visible; possible faint pen mark in red at top right corner (x~1230, y~180).

FACE 1 TILES

image-002 (top strip of face 1; also viewed as my enhanced crops scratchpad/p07/t002a.jpg (blue channel, equalized, whole tile) and t002b.jpg (blue channel, blur+autocontrast, native x200-1700 y200-700)).
Observations: a faint red/brown mark (paragraph sign or initial stroke?) at the far left above line 1 (x~120, y~100 displayed). The text block's left edge is at about x 210 (displayed); lines 1-3 are the best preserved on the face, darker brown; the rest of the strip is almost effaced; a crease runs diagonally from top centre to bottom right. A ruled vertical bounding line/fold at the far right (x~1960). Line numbers count text lines from the top of this tile.
image-002 l.1: h(?) . ia(?) ger(?)ch(?)[...] nemi(?)[illegible to right]   - first letter tall, h or ff/R? then a point; "ia" or "1a"; very uncertain
image-002 l.2: lo(?)' in eo cum o pace .   [rest of line illegible]   - "lo" with superscript stroke (abbrev.); "o pace" (or "opace"/"o(m)pace") appears underlined by a thin line under the letters; point after it
image-002 l.3: [..] Plen(?)itam(?) fu(?) bu(?)ss(?)eram(?) [illegible]   - first word begins with a tall capital (P/D?), slightly indented after two faint letters at left; readings below word level unreliable
image-002 l.4: (indented, x~450) [.]ium(?) [illegible]
image-002 l.5-9: traces of ink across the full line width; individual words not recoverable on this tile at this resolution. l.6 begins (x~210) "[..]um" ; l.7 begins "[.]i[.]ng(?)" ; l.9 begins with a small red/brown mark at x~265 (paragraph sign?).
Limitations: lines 4-9 unread beyond letter traces.

image-003 (second strip of face 1; also enhanced crop scratchpad/p07/t003a.jpg, native x200-2450 y360-960). Overlaps the bottom of image-002 at the top (its first one or two lines are the faint l.8-9 of image-002 - not counted as new text).
Observations: a blue outlined letter (B or E shape, ~200 px tall, drawn in thin blue strokes, not filled) sits in the middle of the strip over lines 4-6, superimposed on the brown text; it looks like a later mark or offset rather than a planned initial (no space left for it in the text). Text block left edge x~190 (displayed), right edge ~x 1830, where a dark vertical band (fold/ruling) runs. Small brown blots/paragraph marks at left at l.2 (x~265) and near the bottom (x~880, y~870).
Line numbering from top of this tile (l.1 = first fully visible line at y~50):
image-003 l.1: [.]ili(?)[...] [illegible] ... [..]o[..] (right, x~1350)
image-003 l.2: (brown mark) [illegible across line]
image-003 l.3: [illegible]
image-003 l.4: non n(?) . a(?)pe(?)[..]e(?) [illegible] ...   - "non" clear at line start
image-003 l.5: bis(?)s(?)[...] [illegible] ... [..]g(?)e [..]   - "bi" with tall ascender at line start
image-003 l.6: hu(?)[...] [..]e(?)[..]n(?) [..]o(?)[..] [illegible] ... [..]an(?)tie(?)[..]
image-003 l.7: [..]t(?) [illegible] in(?)ture(?)[..]   [..]itu[..]ue(?) [..]ure(?) [..]   - very uncertain
image-003 l.8: [..]a(?)c(?)os(?) natu(?)re(?)  l(?)ic(?)e(?)t(?) . in q(ui)b(us)(?) [..]   - "q" with descender and abbreviation stroke, read as q(ui)b(us)? or "q(uo)d"?; uncertain
image-003 l.9: (indented) [..]e(?)[..]i[..] [illegible] ... [..]e[..]io (right end)
image-003 l.10-12: traces only; [illegible]
Limitations: the middle of this strip is badly abraded; only line openings and scattered letters are visible.

image-004 (third strip of face 1; also enhanced crop scratchpad/p07/t004a.jpg, native x150-2450 y350-1000). Overlaps image-003 at top (the brown blot at top x~880 is the one at the bottom of image-003).
Observations: the brown text here is almost completely effaced - only rows of letter-shaped stains (about 12 lines) across the block. Superimposed over the middle are large, later-looking strokes in a greyer/darker ink: long diagonal strokes forming large letters (an "M"/"N"-like group at x 500-1000, y 30-450; a large looped letter, "Q"/"O"/"g"-like, at x 1000-1250, y 450-700; a "Cr"/"Gr"-like group at x 520-700, y 560-650). These look like pen trials or a large later inscription, not the book hand.
Brown text, best guesses only:
image-004 l.~8 (y~410), right portion x~1380-1630: g(?)' acia(?) / "g(ra)cia(?)" - superscript stroke after g
image-004 l.~12 (y~660), right portion x~1400-1600: [.]o(?)ue(?) / "Deo(?)" - uncertain
All other lines: [illegible] (traces only).
Limitations: nothing connected is readable on this strip.

image-005 (bottom strip of face 1). Overlaps image-004 at top.
Observations: ink here survives only as pale "ghost" letter shapes (ink eaten away, leaving lighter letter forms) in about 10 lines; text block left edge x~170 (displayed). Tear at bottom right; folded strip at right edge with no legible text.
image-005 l.1 (y~70): aut(?)[..]  [..] [..]ilio(?)[..]e(?) [illegible] ... [..]n(?)
image-005 l.2 (y~160): e[.] [..] [..]n(?)[..]  [illegible]
image-005 l.3 (y~245), indented x~560: [.]ul(?)ti(?)tudi(?)ne(?)[..]  [illegible]   - word with ascenders "lt" then "tud"; very uncertain
image-005 l.4 (y~330): [illegible] ... [..]ri(?)[..]
image-005 l.5 (y~420): [..]ui(?)m(?)ab(?)[..]  [..]ru(?)m(?) [illegible]
image-005 l.6 (y~520): [..]e[..]  [..]u[..] [..]ni(?)cio(?) [illegible]
image-005 l.7-10: traces only; [illegible]
Limitations: nothing connected is readable on this strip.

Face 2 (overview image-006): parchment leaf, portrait, text block filling nearly the whole width (left edge x~230, running off the right edge at x~1150 on the overview; text continues onto a narrow pale strip at right, x~1150-1170, which seems to be a turned edge). Folded-over strips at top (blank) and bottom (x 150-1070, y 1700-1790): the bottom turn-in carries two lines of better-preserved brown text (upside-down relative to nothing - it reads the right way up), e.g. "...p(re)ndit(?) applicatu(m)..." visible on the overview. A small blue painted mark at top-left corner (x~150, y~190) with a thin red line running right from it (possibly the tip of a blue initial with red pen-flourish, or a paraph). A red/brown vertical stroke at x~790, y 300-430 (stain or rubric stroke). About 38-40 lines of a single column in a small Gothic book hand, long lines, very faded and stained; middle lines (y~880-1200) a little darker. No running title visible. Ruling not visible.

FACE 2 TILES

image-007 (top strip of face 2; also enhanced crop scratchpad/p07/t007a.jpg, native x250-2950 y230-1158 - enhancement did not add legible words).
Observations: blue mark at extreme top-left corner (x~40, y~0). Top ~170 px of the strip blank/abraded (upper margin). Text begins y~200 (displayed) with ~7 lines visible across the full width (left edge x~200, right edge x~1910 at a dark vertical line, which looks like a fold or the text-block bound). A red-brown vertical stroke with a blob at the top (x 1210-1330, y 160-430) crosses lines 1-3: looks like a drip/stain, not a letter. Small red dot x~1150 y~540.
image-007 l.1 (y~210): [.]E(?)[..] [illegible] ... [..]o pa(?)rt(?)i(?)s(?) / "...o p(ar)tis(?)" at right end (x~1720-1880)
image-007 l.2 (y~295): [illegible] ... [..]e(?)s(?) [..] i[..]e(?) ... [..]ine(?) / right end "[..]ane(?)"
image-007 l.3 (y~375): [illegible] ... [..] [..]n(?) (right)
image-007 l.4 (y~450): [illegible] [..]nus(?)[..] (centre, x~1200) ... [..]a(?) (right)
image-007 l.5 (y~520): [illegible]
image-007 l.6 (y~600): [..]o(?)n(?)o(?)r(?)a(?)[..] (x~380-560) [illegible]
image-007 l.7 (y~680): [illegible] [..]u(?)ab(?)u(?)la(?)n(?)tie(?)[..]  (x~720-1170) [illegible] ... [..]c(?)ti(?)a(?) (right)
Limitations: practically no connected text.

image-008 (second strip of face 2; enhanced crop scratchpad/p07/t008a.jpg, native x200-2950 y480-1180). Overlaps image-007 at top (its first line ~y 60 = image-007 l.7).
Observations: ~11 lines visible; faint horizontal ruling lines visible at y~315, ~545, ~620 (displayed) - dry-point/plummet ruling; left text edge x~170, right bound at dark vertical line x~1890; letters extending past it on the right (x 1900-1960) on several lines (e.g. "m", "n" at y~200, "y"/"g" at y~380) - text continuing onto the turned edge strip.

Observations: best-preserved part of face 2. ~12 lines. Ruling lines visible (y~40, ~565 displayed). Dark vertical bound at x~1890; letters spill beyond it at right. Lines 5 and 6 begin indented (x~250-350) - possibly paragraph/lemma openings, or just abrasion at the left; can't tell. A curved scratch/crease loops across l.6-10 (x 790-960). Darker ink spots: "hic loq" (l.5), "...mg u(e)l" (l.7), ". i ." (l.8), "f" (l.8), which look like the original darker ink where the surface is less worn.

image-009 l.5 (y~385), starts x~250: [..] ʒ(?)ma(?) hic loq(uitur)(?) [..]u(?)a(?)[..]  [illegible]   - "hic loq" fairly clear (dark ink), with abbreviation over/after q not resolved; preceded by "...ma" or "...ina"

This tile ends above the folded bottom strip seen on the overview (image-006 y 1700-1790), so that turn-in with its two better-preserved lines is NOT covered by any tile (see crop below).

Face 3 (overview image-011): parchment leaf, portrait, far better preserved than faces 1-2. Brown ink, small Gothic textualis with dense abbreviation; points used as separators around short abbreviated groups (citation-like strings such as "· di · c ·", "· q · ii ·"). END OF READING
Overall limitations and notes:
- Faces 1 and 2 are almost wholly effaced; only isolated words were recoverable even with blue-channel contrast enhancement. Faces 3 and 4 are legible in part; face 3 (image-011..015) gives the most connected text (single column, ~41 lines, a red/blue decorated initial in the left margin, red marginal rubric "Decr(?)" and top-right red letters).
- On faces 3 and 4 the text is a densely abbreviated prose with frequent strings of points around short abbreviated groups and numerals (e.g. ". lxxvij . d .", ". q . iij .", ". i . c . i ."), the recurring abbreviated phrase "in glo." , the "8"-shaped sign before "c"/"e", and words in larger script ("sacros ordines", "allegans", "regulis sacris", "si quis", "dispensabiles"(?)). I take these as observations only; I have not tried to identify the text.
- Numerals are uncertain everywhere (x/l and long final j are easily confused at this wear).
- Line numbers are counted from the top of each tile; overlaps with the previous tile are flagged and not counted as new text. The "[f3 l.N]"/"[f4 l.N]" face-line numbers are my running estimate and may be off by one.
- Fold-strip letters on face 4 are given in braces and may be misaligned with their lines.
- Areas not covered at native resolution: the bottom turn-in of face 2 (overview only; native image would help) and the bottom turn-in of face 3 was read from tile 015 (fine). Faces 1 and 2 would benefit from UV or multispectral imaging.
